brief:
Palestinian women in Gaza are accepting unfavorable divorce settlements to avoid lengthy court proceedings, according to Al Jazeera English. The practice reflects deepening legal obstacles that make formal divorce processes costly and time-consuming, leaving women with limited recourse to resolve matrimonial disputes quickly.

Women seeking divorce face systemic barriers within Gaza's court system that discourage formal legal action. Many are choosing instead to negotiate settlements that strip them of claims to property, custody arrangements, and financial support. The legal bottlenecks have created a pattern in which women prioritize speed of dissolution over protection of their own interests, effectively forcing them to relinquish substantive rights in exchange for faster resolution of marriage disputes.
dek: Amid legal struggles, Gaza women opt for quicker divorces, sacrificing rights to escape prolonged court battles.
title: Gaza women surrender rights to escape prolonged divorce battles.
